tldr: DeepSeek's flagship V4 Pro entered late July already under scrutiny, benchmarked head-to-head against Kimi K3 and GLM-5.2 on cost, license, and serving price. Within days a rival low-cost model was already undercutting it on price-performance, and by July 31 DeepSeek's own retrained V4-Flash sibling was beating Pro on nine agent benchmarks.
whats_new: A Pandaily write-up (Aug 3) puts a number on the official V4-Flash release — 304B parameters — and claims it matches Claude Opus-4.8, dubbing it DeepSeek's "third DeepSeek moment."
why_it_matters: If the Opus-4.8 comparison holds up under independent testing, V4-Flash isn't just a cheaper fallback — it's a credible frontier-class option at a fraction of the cost, which changes the make-vs-buy math for agent workloads currently pinned to a premium model.

status.detail: V4-Flash is officially released at 304B params; the newest coverage claims it matches Claude Opus-4.8, though that comparison is still self-reported/syndicated.

beats.headline: V4 Pro benchmarked against Kimi K3 and GLM-5.2 on cost, license, and performance
beats.summary: A three-way trillion-scale MoE comparison put V4 Pro alongside two open-weight rivals on benchmarks, licensing terms, and serving cost.

beats.headline: Rival Laguna S 2.1 undercuts V4 Pro on price and performance
beats.summary: A newly released low-cost model was pitched as cheaper than DeepSeek's own V4-Flash and better than V4 Pro.

beats.headline: V4-Flash ships officially and beats flagship Pro on nine agent benchmarks
beats.summary: DeepSeek's retrained, cheaper sibling model goes from research claim to official release and now outperforms Pro on agent-focused evaluations.

beats.headline: Outside press frames V4-Flash's affordability as the story
beats.summary: Independent coverage picks up V4-Flash as the notable, cost-effective option rather than treating Pro as DeepSeek's flagship story.

beats.headline: 304B V4-Flash claimed to match Claude Opus-4.8, called DeepSeek's "third DeepSeek moment"
beats.summary: Chinese-tech coverage specifies the model's parameter count for the first time and puts its capability on par with Anthropic's flagship, framing this alongside DeepSeek's two prior industry-shaking releases.

open_questions: Does an independent, third-party eval confirm V4-Flash genuinely matches Claude Opus-4.8, or is that comparison self-reported by DeepSeek and relayed uncritically?
Does DeepSeek reposition V4-Flash as the default choice for agent workloads, or keep Pro as the flagship despite the benchmark loss?
Do independent evals confirm V4-Flash's nine-benchmark lead over Pro, or is this still DeepSeek's own reported result?
take_for_builders: Before swapping in V4-Flash on the strength of the Opus-4.8 comparison, rerun your own agent-benchmark suite against it — the parity claim is still syndicated coverage of DeepSeek's own numbers, not an independent eval.
